_doc: Latency budgets for the engine's own nightly-measurable benchmarks (Phase 66). Each budget names its owner criterion group/id under crates/krishiv-bench/benches/ so scripts/bench-tier.sh knows where to read target/criterion/<path>/new/estimates.json. The gate (scripts/bench_gate.py, ported from the platform repo's Phase 29) flags results exceeding budget by >20% on two consecutive nightly runs. Units: milliseconds unless noted. TPC-H budgets are declared under `"tier": "tpch"` and are evaluated ONLY by `scripts/bench-tpch-tier.sh --tier tpch` on a host that has the dataset; the nightly job passes `--tier nightly` so `--require-fresh` never fails on them. TPC-DS is still excluded entirely:  those benches need KRISHIV_TPCH_DATA_DIR_*/KRISHIV_TPCDS_DATA_DIR pointing at multi-GB generated data that CI does not provision, so they self-skip today (see BENCHMARKING.md's 'What this gate does not cover yet') rather than being declared here and permanently failing --require-fresh for an infrastructure reason, not a performance one.

documented target < 5ms; met at ~142us after the streaming_latency rewrite (was MISSED at 11.7ms, a benchmark-methodology artifact of measuring one-time RocksDB-open cost as if it were per-batch cost, not a real engine regression — see BENCHMARKING.md)
